## Copying what you actually selected

- **Ctrl+C no longer copies a different message.** Selecting text in a streamed answer and copying it often put text from an earlier message on the clipboard. The cause was in the terminal toolkit: a selection is remembered as row and column coordinates and re-read against whatever the rows contain *now*, so a stream chunk, a markdown finalize or the swap from streaming text to final markdown between mouse-up and Ctrl+C changed what your selection meant. PiTTy now takes a snapshot of the selected text the moment the selection finishes, and copies that. The prompt editor's own selection is untouched. This is a fix on our side of a toolkit limitation, so one narrow race remains: text that arrives in the moment between the final selection pass and your mouse-up can still be taken from the newer content.

## A child's thinking stays readable

- **Streamed reasoning is kept after a child stops.** PiTTy only read the child's live event stream while it was running, so the moment a child finished, its streamed thinking was thrown away — even though for most providers that stream is the *only* plaintext reasoning that exists (the session file stores reasoning encrypted, with the text stripped). The stream is now read for finished children too, and merged into the displayed transcript instead of shown twice.
- **A child's trace no longer reshuffles while it loads.** Transcript rows were identified by their position in a rolling window, so every refresh invented new identities and every row was destroyed and rebuilt — scroll jumps, blocks collapsing on their own, and text overlapping while it re-laid out. Row identity is now stable across refreshes.
- **Tools keep their descriptions.** Tool rows coming from the live stream had no arguments recorded, so they appeared as a bare `TOOL · read` with nothing after the name. PiTTy now fills those in from the session file's matching tool call — the same row shows its command, path or arguments again.

## Overlapping text

- **Sidebar rows no longer overlap.** A row calculated its third line and its height once, when it was created. A child that began reporting tool activity therefore kept the shorter height, and its new line overlapped the row below or left a hole. Both now follow the content.
- **Message bubbles no longer fight over their own visibility.** Two writers set the same property — one in code, one in the layout — and disagreed for a frame on every transition, which could show both the streaming text and its final markdown at once, or neither. There is one owner per property now.

## Also in this release

- The three copies of the "is this a subagent tool?" rule had drifted apart, so `task_*` tools looked like agents without being groupable and `workflow_*` tools grouped without the agent styling. They share one rule again, and a subagent row that cannot derive a summary shows its arguments instead of nothing.
- Removed several places where display values were guessed rather than reported: a finished child's rows no longer measure time from the epoch, a timeout in milliseconds is no longer reinterpreted as seconds, and a "×N children" badge can no longer be conjured from coincidental JSON in a tool's output.

## Validation

- PiTTy typecheck passed; complete local suite: **467 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed**; type-escape scan clean. Each behaviour fix has a test that fails against the previous code.
